items.title: As you add more independent factors, how misleading does the naive worst-case bound become?
items.description: Each factor here could independently run anywhere from half your guess to double it (matching L2's 3-factor table). This sweeps the number of independent factors in the decomposition and computes the 'typical' middle-50% spread across every corner combination (every possible mix of each factor running high or low), shown as a percentage of the full naive worst-case bound (multiplying every factor's low together, and every factor's high together). Watch it shrink fast: with more independent factors, the naive bound increasingly overstates what's actually likely, because reaching it requires every factor to err the same direction at once.
items.compute: const n = Math.round(params.factorCount); const total = Math.pow(2, n); const vals = []; for (let mask = 0; mask < total; mask++) { let sumLog2 = 0; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { const high = (mask >> i) & 1; sumLog2 += high ? 1 : -1; } vals.push(Math.pow(2, sumLog2)); } vals.sort((a, b) => a - b); function percentile(sorted, p) { const idx = (sorted.length - 1) * p; const lo = Math.floor(idx); const hi = Math.ceil(idx); if (lo === hi) return sorted[lo]; return sorted[lo] + (sorted[hi] - sorted[lo]) * (idx - lo); } const p25 = percentile(vals, 0.25); const p75 = percentile(vals, 0.75); const typicalSpread = p75 / p25; const naiveSpread = Math.pow(4, n); const typicalSharePercent = (typicalSpread / naiveSpread) * 100; return { typicalSharePercent };

outputs.label: Typical (middle-50%) spread, as a share of the naive bound

items.title: How does each factor's own uncertainty affect the final estimate's spread?
items.description: Grounded in L3's storage example: 3 independently-ranged factors (activeUsers, eventsPerUserPerDay, bytesPerEvent), each one's low/high spread controlled here by a single 'uncertainty multiple' -- at the default of about 1.48x, the combined naive worst-case bound spans the same ~10.7x this unit's L3 computed for the real (unequal) factor ranges. Watch how quickly a small increase in per-factor uncertainty widens the combined naive bound, since three factors' spreads all multiply together.

params.name: uncertaintyMultiple
params.label: Each factor's high/low multiple (e.g. 2 = factor could be half or double)

items.compute: const m = params.uncertaintyMultiple; const rangedFactorCount = 3; const naiveSpread = Math.pow(m * m, rangedFactorCount); return { naiveSpread };
